items.title: [next] Exclude never-prerenderable params from allowQuery for blocking app prerenders
items.body:
Cache Components routes whose generateStaticParams only partially covers their params produce blocking prerender entries (no servable fallback) for the param combinations that aren't fully enumerated. These entries emitted allowQuery containing every route param, including params that generateStaticParams can never provide. Since the on-demand render for a blocking entry is cached, this both partitioned the cache by params that should never vary it (a distinct entry per value, e.g. per id) and resolved those params into the cached content, so every subsequent visitor to the shared route was served the first requester's param values as static output.

The cache key contract for these entries is that only prerenderable params may partition the cache: root params (which generateStaticParams is required to provide) and the entry's remainingPrerenderableParams from the prerender manifest. Filtering allowQuery to that set makes the proxy strip the never-prerenderable params from the request, which defers them through the existing params-missing handling so they resume per request against the shared entry. Next.js emits remainingPrerenderableParams for these entries as of 16.3.0-canary.8x and the same filtering already landed in its built-in adapter; builds from versions that don't emit the field are unchanged. This only touches the blocking arm's cache key and does not alter fallback serving semantics.

items.title: feat(build-utils,next): add hasPostponed signal to Prerender
items.body:
## What

Exposes a per-route tri-state **`hasPostponed`** signal on `Prerender`:

- `true` — the route's `.meta` postponed state is present (React suspended during the build-time prerender)
- `false` — a Prerender route that prerendered **without** postponing
- `undefined` — the framework did not provide the signal

This is the source-of-truth answer to *"did React suspend during the build-time prerender for this route?"* — currently only inferable indirectly via `chain` / `experimentalStreamingLambdaPath` presence, which over-reports as PPR under `cacheComponents: true` (PPR machinery exists even for fully-static routes).

## Changes

**`@vercel/build-utils`** (`prerender.ts`)
- Add optional `hasPostponed?: boolean` to `PrerenderOptions` and as a public `Prerender` field.
- Store it **unconditionally** so the tri-state round-trips intact — the existing boolean idiom (`partialFallback`/`exposeErrBody`/`passQuery`) collapses `false` into `undefined`, which would defeat the signal.

**`@vercel/next`** (`utils.ts`)
- Compute `Boolean(postponedState)` inside the existing `PARTIALLY_STATIC && appDir && !isBlocking` block and pass it to all four `new Prerender(...)` sites (HTML page, data/prefetch, dynamic-RSC chain, segment).
- Pages-router and other non-app-router prerenders leave it `undefined`.

This is **additive** — it does not touch the existing `chain` / `experimentalStreamingLambdaPath` logic. Downstream consumers can now distinguish a route that actually postponed from one that has PPR machinery but fully prerendered (e.g. under `cacheComponents: true`).

## Tests

Tested it in this deployment https://vercel.com/curated-tests/o11y-playground-app-with-cache-components/AUUKS8MDrwbzWmLkLs7XD27VL8hr

items.title: Unable to read URL query parameters in Prerender Functions
items.body:
I stumbled upon an undocumented behaviour while working on [vite-plugin-vercel](https://github.com/magne4000/vite-plugin-vercel).
Currently, using Output API v3, Prerender Functions does not seem to be forwarding URL query parameters correctly to the underlying function.

Take the following route from `config.json#routes`:
```json
{
  "src": "^(/isr)$",
  "dest": "/pages/isr-QfOiv5trhLiUQCBvSSmPl/?__original_path=$1",
  "check": true
},
```

With the following function configs:
```json5
// .vc-config.json
{
  "runtime": "nodejs20.x",
  "handler": "index.js",
  "launcherType": "Nodejs",
  "shouldAddHelpers": true
}

// isr-QfOiv5trhLiUQCBvSSmPl.prerender-config.json
{
  "expiration": 15,
  "group": 3
}
```

Now I try to go to `/isr?someQuery=value`, and in my handler I `console.log(request.query)`, the object is always empty (`{}`).

For simple Serverless non-Prerender Functions, the query is NOT empty.

I cannot verify my claim, but I think that it was working in the past.


### `passQuery` parameter

I just saw that there is a documented [passQuery](https://vercel.com/docs/build-output-api/v3/primitives#prerender-configuration-file) option now.
I tried to play with it but I have no idea how it works. There is no example, and [searching for `passQuery` in your whole codebase](https://github.com/search?q=org%3Avercel%20passQuery&type=code) only points to the [initial PR adding it](https://github.com/vercel/vercel/pull/9388), with references to a Slack no one has access to.

Adding `passQuery: true` in my `isr-QfOiv5trhLiUQCBvSSmPl.prerender-config.json` makes the function always fail with a 500 error. This error does not show anywhere in the logs.
[I have an opened PR testing this param](https://github.com/magne4000/vite-plugin-vercel/pull/50).

---

So I have 2 question:
- Should my first use case work (i.e. have access to query parameters in a Prerender Function)? I would suspect so because the `allowQuery` option wouldn't make much sense.
- What does `passQuery` do, and how should we use it? I have the feeling that it could simplify my integration, as it seems to be a replacement for the undocumented `x-now-route-matches` header

items.title: [next] Enable passQuery flag for Next.js prerenders
items.body:
This enables the `passQuery` field for the Prerenders we output in Next.js since Next.js has already supported consuming the route matches from the query for a long time we just never flipped it on. 

Fixes https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/71757

items.title: [build-utils] Add passQuery field to Prerender
items.body:
This adds a new `passQuery` field to `Prerender` outputs to allow opting into new behavior for passing query/route matches in the URL instead of the `x-now-route-matches` header.
